subject: Materials Science
title: Ceramic Degradation: Slow but Sure
description: A micro-lesson that makes Ceramic Degradation: Slow but Sure usable.

hook.text: Ancient Roman concrete still stands — but the Portland cement in your driveway is already cracking at 30 years.

buildup.text: Ceramics resist corrosion well — but they degrade through chemical dissolution, hydration, and phase changes.

discovery.text: Concrete degrades when water carries chloride ions to the rebar — the steel corrodes and expands, cracking the concrete.

twist.text: Silicon nitride, used in bearings, degrades slowly in water at high temperature — even ceramics have limits.

climax.text: Understanding ceramic degradation lets engineers predict lifetimes of dental implants and reactor containments.

punchline.text: Ceramics outlast metals in most environments — but nothing lasts forever.

quiz.question: How does reinforced concrete typically degrade?
options: Chlorides reach rebar, causing corrosion that cracks the concrete from inside
